sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 3890 of 2024
Applicant :- Dilip Kumar @ Sonu
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Abrar Ahmad

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by the applicant is taken on record.

2. The State with its counter affidavit has enclosed a copy of the information given to the opposite party no.2/complainant, however, despite service of notice, opposite party no.2 is not represented by any counsel.

3. Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Dilip Kumar @ Sonu for grant of bail, in Case Crime No.777 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 D(A) I.P.C. and Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Police Station Thakurganj, District Lucknow,,
during trial.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.
6.

It is further submitted that the allegations against the applicant are in terms that he had enticed away the prosecutrix aged about 13-14 years, however, the case of the prosecution is belied by the statement of the prosecutrix recorded before the trial court.

Elaborating further, it is submitted that the age of the prosecutrix as per admitted case of the prosecution is shown as 17 years and 03 months and in the F.I.R., she is shown to have been enticed away by the applicant on 06.11.2023,
however, she herself appeared before the concerned police station on 07.11.2023 and has been given in the custody of her mother and though in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., she alleged the allegation of rape against the applicant, but the same are not corroborated by any medical evidence as no sign of force suggesting any sexual assault has been found on her person.
7.

It is further submitted that in her statement recorded before the trial court, the prosecutrix has categorically admitted to be in love with the applicant and also that she is not intending to convict the applicant as she was in love with him and they were known to each other since long.

8. Highlighting the above facts, it is vehemently submitted that the prosecutrix was a consenting party as she has not sustained any injury and admitted to have accompanied the applicant on her own wish and volition.

The relationship of the applicant with the prosecutrix may only be termed as a consensual relationship of two willing persons and would not amount to rape in absence of any concrete proof with regard to age of the prosecutrix, which is yet to be decided/assessed finally by the trial court in the trial.

9. It is next submitted that applicant is in jail in this case since 13.11.2023 and having regard to the pace with the trial is going on, the same is not going to conclude in near future, charge-sheet in this case has already been submitted and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail the applicant may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
10.

Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and having regard to the material/evidence available against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail, but could not controvert the other factual submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant.
11. Considering the facts that the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
has also accused the co-accused Vipin Kumar (who has already been released on anticipatory bail)
subjecting him to rape along with the applicant, no injury or any abnormality has been noticed on the person of the prosecutrix during the course of her medical examination and the text and tenor of the application given by the mother of the prosecutrix at the police station at the time of taking her into her custody, wherein it is stated that the prosecutrix was not subjected to physical assault as also the statement of the prosecutrix recorded before the trial court, wherein she has almost exonerated the applicant and also considering the age of the prosecutrix as well as of the applicant at Dilip Kumar @ Sonu vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167915923/
2 the relevant point of time, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail. The bail application is thus allowed.
12. Let the accused/applicant- Dilip Kumar @ Sonu involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.

sentences.text: ( ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
13. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
14. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
15. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression of this Court on the merits of the case.
